lead.headline: ₹18,690 CRORE PM-KISAN INSTALMENT SET FOR 9.34 CRORE FARMERS TODAY
lead.deck: The 24th transfer is scheduled for 9 am from Banaskantha, Gujarat, with new farm infrastructure initiatives also announced
paragraphs: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to release the 24th PM-KISAN instalment at a programme in Banaskantha, Gujarat, at 9 am today. More than 9.34 crore farmers are set to receive over ₹18,690 crore through direct benefit transfer.

The Agriculture Ministry said 521 Agriculture Infrastructure Fund units will also be dedicated and 12 horticulture clusters inaugurated to strengthen storage, processing and high-value crop production.
Eligible beneficiaries receive the instalment directly in their bank accounts. The official PM-KISAN portal says e-KYC is mandatory for registered farmers.

sidebarStory.headline: BENGALURU METRO PINK LINE CLEARED FOR ELEVATED STRETCH
sidebarStory.subhead: Safety approval covers 7.5 km; the opening date has not yet been confirmed
paragraphs: The Commissioner of Metro Railway Safety has cleared the 7.5-km elevated section between Kalena Agrahara and Tavarekere. The state is awaiting an inauguration date; a public opening has not been announced.

stories.headline: PINK LINE GETS SAFETY CLEARANCE; OPENING DATE AWAITS
stories.subhead: CMRS approval applies to Bengaluru’s 7.5-km elevated stretch
paragraphs: The elevated section between Kalena Agrahara and Tavarekere has received statutory safety clearance. Karnataka has asked the Union government to confirm an inauguration date; November 15 has been discussed but is not confirmed.

stories.headline: OUTSTATION FUEL TANKERS TO BYPASS BENGALURU FROM NOVEMBER 1
stories.subhead: Dealers’ body says tankers serving outlets outside the city will be routed away from city roads
paragraphs: Petroleum tankers carrying fuel to destinations outside Bengaluru are to bypass city roads from November 1, according to the dealers’ association. The change is aimed at reducing heavy tanker movement through the city.

stories.headline: KARNATAKA RECORDS 702 SNAKEBITES IN A WEEK
paragraphs: As snake sightings rise in Bengaluru homes and neighbourhoods, Karnataka recorded 702 snakebite cases and six deaths in a week. The state has registered 17,608 cases and 205 deaths since January, according to figures cited in the report.

stories.headline: ISRO TO LAUNCH NAVIGATION SATELLITE NVS-03 TONIGHT
paragraphs: ISRO plans to launch NVS-03 aboard the GSLV-F18 from Sriharikota at 11:51 pm IST. The satellite is part of the next-generation navigation series intended to maintain services from India’s regional NavIC system.

stories.headline: SUPREME COURT SEEKS CENTRE’S REPLY ON PRIVACY LAW CHALLENGE
paragraphs: The Supreme Court issued notice to the Centre on a challenge by the Digital News Publishers Association to parts of the data-protection law. The petition argues the provisions lack safeguards for journalistic work and confidential sources.

stories.headline: SNAKE SIGHTINGS RISE IN BENGALURU AS KARNATAKA LOGS 702 BITES
stories.deck: More than 200 rescue requests reportedly came in over three days as snakes entered homes and residential areas
paragraphs: Snake-rescue calls have risen across Bengaluru as reptiles are reported in homes and around everyday household spaces. More than 200 calls to civic, police and fire helplines were reported over three days.

Karnataka recorded 702 snakebite cases and six deaths in the past week. The report says 17,608 cases and 205 deaths have been recorded statewide since January; residents are urged to keep distance and call trained rescuers.

stories.headline: PINK LINE CLEARED, BUT METRO OPENING DATE IS NOT SET
paragraphs: Safety clearance covers the 7.5-km elevated corridor between Kalena Agrahara and Tavarekere. The state says it is ready to begin service once the inauguration date is confirmed.

stories.headline: FUEL TANKERS BOUND OUTSIDE CITY TO BYPASS BENGALURU
paragraphs: The dealers’ body says tankers supplying fuel to areas beyond Bengaluru will be routed away from city roads starting November 1.

stories.headline: INDIA EYES 4-0 LEAD IN AUCKLAND T20I TODAY
stories.deck: The fourth match against New Zealand begins at Eden Park at 12:30 pm IST
paragraphs: India, leading the five-match series 3-0, meets New Zealand in the fourth T20I at Auckland’s Eden Park on Friday. The match is scheduled to begin at 12:30 pm IST.
Ishan Kishan is nearing a return from injury, leaving India with a selection decision at the top of the order, while New Zealand is without injured seamers Lockie Ferguson and Matt Henry.

stories.headline: NVS-03 SET FOR GSLV-F18 LAUNCH FROM SRIHARIKOTA
paragraphs: The navigation satellite carries atomic clocks and an L1 signal in addition to L5 and S-band signals, according to ISRO. The launch is planned for 11:51 pm IST on Friday.
